mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where UNRATE drops below 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% signals elevated precautionary savings behavior by households, which reduces disposable income available for consumption and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months where RSAFS rises by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is inconsistent with normal labor market dynamics and signals potential data inconsistency or a structural break, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10%.
